notes: Device registrations: where each device's TOOL TIP is, expressed in the axis
space of the device the camera rides on (ref_device). Given a pose h on the
registered device, its tip is at  p_ref = R * h + offset  -- and the pose that
puts the tip at a point is  h = R^T * (p_ref - offset).
Everything is in RAW AXIS coordinates of the two named devices. This is the
same rule the needle offset follows and for the same reason: a pick already
reports there, read_position reads there, move_axis_to commands there, and
gantry-main's entry in motion_transforms.json inverts Z - so a number that
took a detour through the axis transform would descend where it meant to
retreat.
R IS NOT MEASURED. It is the permutation implied by motion_transforms.json,
composed as M_ref * M_dev^T and adopted when the tip is first taught -
rotation_source records that. Those entries are hand-typed +-1 matrices: exact
for a device bolted square, approximate otherwise, and the error vanishes at
the point the tip was taught and grows with distance from it. That is a fair
deal for an APPROACH, and the CHECK is the only thing that ever puts a number
on what it costs - which is why it drives away from the taught pose.
offset (t) IS measured, by imprint: touch the tool onto a coupon, mark the
corners of the mark it leaves, and the centre is the tip in XY while the
focused camera Z over the coupon is the tip in Z. There is no separate dz
field: a reference Z here already means the gantry Z that focuses on a thing.
This file SHIPS EMPTY. Teach each tool-carrying device on the Registration
page (F8): capture the imprint pose, the home pose and the camera view, mark
the corners, compute - then run the check.
A completed registration is written to config/device_reg.local.json, which is
gitignored and loads in preference to this file. Do not hand-edit that one -
the Registration page shows it, re-measures it, and checks it.
Two dates, and the difference matters: registered_at is when the rotation was
adopted; tip_taught_at is the last time the offset was measured. R belongs to
the MOUNT, offset belongs to the mount AND the tool - so changing a gripper
invalidates one imprint's worth of the record, not the whole thing.
